title: Why Thomas's band feels like home; Manuel and Joe James
summary: Collins and Penn praise the band's closeness, Manuel Paul's love of playing, and Joe James singing blues.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Some time ago, Mr. Bill, you asked me to Sam's question about that. Why is it that I seem to be more happier with Thomas than with the rest of the men? You asked me that. Well I feel very much there at home with him. You see, with that bunch of men. That's really why.

You can tell they all, like Sammy says, they all love music too. That's right, that's right. I always say that about Manuel too. He never puts his horn down. You can't stop him. Sometimes the band stops and he'll start all the piece by himself. He'll start all the piece by himself. He just won't stop playing.

He just loves music. He's ready, that's right. That's right. You take like Joe James. I like to hear Joe sing sometimes, but sometimes he won't sing when I want him to sing. He won't sing for me, you know. Just that time he feel good he'll sing. I like the way he sings.
I've only ever heard him sing the blues. Does he sing anything else?
Well, he used to sing a few numbers all the time, but he just lately just sing blues now. He's a blues singer.
I guess he's been feeling rather unwell. Yeah.
I believe that has plenty to do with it. Probably does. Yeah, it has plenty to do with it.
